claim: UpGuard published the Power Apps portal disclosure on 23 August 2021.
Power Apps portal lists with OData enabled exposed data anonymously unless table permissions were enabled on the list as well as the table.
locator: Background paragraphs beginning One of the options and When a developer enables
evidence: OData feed plus list setting; table permissions ignored by list until enabled
qualification: This is a configuration interaction, not evidence that every portal list was exposed.

claim: List table permissions were disabled by default at the time; Microsoft later changed the default for newly created portals.
locator: Background paragraph beginning Power Apps Portals lists; Microsoft Response paragraph beginning Additionally
evidence: all lists having table permissions disabled by default; newly created portals will have them enabled
qualification: The source describes the change as planned in Microsoft Response and as completed in Conclusion; avoid a precise rollout date.

claim: The article quotes Microsoft documentation requiring table permissions on the table and Enable Table Permissions on the list.
evidence: To secure a list configure Table Permissions and set Enable Table Permissions true
qualification: Quoted by UpGuard from Microsoft's documentation, not independently archived documentation.

claim: UpGuard first discovered an exposed OData list on 24 May 2021 and found lists by subdomain enumeration search engines and the _odata endpoint.
locator: Discovery paragraphs beginning On May 24 and First we identified and After identifying
evidence: May 24; three portal domains; /_odata lists names; individual list returns rows or forbidden

claim: UpGuard reported examples to MSRC on 24 June 2021 and says Microsoft closed the case on 29 June as by design.
locator: Vulnerability disclosure to Microsoft paragraphs beginning On Thursday June 24 and Over the next day
qualification: The by-design sentence is Microsoft as quoted by UpGuard.

claim: UpGuard says it found over a thousand anonymously accessible lists across a few hundred portals and notified 47 entities involving 38 million records.
locator: Introduction paragraph beginning UpGuard notified; Notification to affected entities opening
evidence: 47 entities; 38 million records; over a thousand lists
qualification: UpGuard totals; not a count of confirmed malicious access.

claim: The exposed examples UpGuard sent to MSRC included government COVID-19 portals and a job-applicant portal with Social Security numbers.
locator: Vulnerability disclosure to Microsoft paragraph beginning On Thursday June 24
evidence: COVID-19 tracing or vaccination; applicant SSNs
qualification: Examples in UpGuard's report to Microsoft.

claim: UpGuard says the Global Payroll Services list had 332000 records including names Microsoft email addresses phone numbers and employee IDs; it was no longer public by 16 July after a 15 July abuse report.
locator: Abuse report to Microsoft paragraphs beginning On Friday July 16; Significant Microsoft portals Global Payroll Services
evidence: 332000; abuse report July 15; no longer public by July 16
qualification: Do not infer the exact time the list was made private.

claim: UpGuard reports Microsoft released a Portal Checker and planned default-enabled table permissions for new portals; UpGuard agrees the issue was not strictly a software vulnerability.
locator: Microsoft Response paragraph beginning Additionally; Conclusion paragraph beginning While we understand
evidence: Portal Checker; newly created portals; not strictly software vulnerability
qualification: Do not assert a dated completed rollout from this article alone.
